title_clean: The Many Kinds or Elements (MN 115) - Paṭicca Samuppāda Part 6
description_short: Bhante explores the middle stages of dependent origination, from contact through grasping, revealing the crucial escape point between feeling and craving.
description_long:
In this continuation of his series on paṭicca samuppāda (dependent origination), Bhante Bodhidhamma examines the crucial middle stages of the twelve-link chain that lead from contact to suffering. Drawing from the Bahudhātuka Sutta (MN 115), he explains how contact between sense base, object, and consciousness gives rise to vedanā (feeling) - the pleasant, unpleasant, or neutral quality of experience.

The talk reveals the pivotal moment between vedanā and taṇhā (craving) where liberation becomes possible. Bhante describes how feelings naturally arise, but suffering only occurs when we move from simple wanting to the identity-based 'I want' of upādāna (grasping). He explores the four types of grasping, particularly sakkāya-diṭṭhi (personality view), and demonstrates how meditation practice allows us to observe this process moment by moment.

Using practical examples like dealing with an itch during meditation, Bhante shows how awareness can interrupt the automatic progression from contact to suffering. The teaching concludes with the reverse process - how the cessation of ignorance leads to the complete ending of this mass of dukkha, offering hope for genuine liberation through understanding and practice.
